pending.body: The fallback_all_co2 path (chemistry.rs:85-92) reports all DIC as CO2 with zero HCO3-/CO3--, yet the pH is computed from acid_only_fallback_ph which implies nonzero HCO3-. At the clamped pH of 5.5, HCO3- should be ~12% of CO2 (10^(5.5-6.35) ≈ 0.14). The species output is thermodynamically inconsistent with the reported pH. This causes bicarbonate_mg_total to be artificially zeroed in low-alkalinity water, slightly distorting TDS/conductivity for those regimes. Fix: call carbonate_species_for_ph at the solved (clamped) pH instead of hardcoding all DIC as CO2, or document why the inconsistency is acceptable.

The design contract (docs/carbonate_state_contract.md line 112) specifies that fallback paths should 'emit a structured diagnostic' when triggered. The implementation in fallback_all_co2, fallback_high_buffer, and fallback_outside_quadratic_envelope (chemistry.rs:85-118) silently returns results without any logging or tracing. Add at minimum a tracing::debug! or equivalent so operators can detect when the solver hits edge cases during gameplay.

No integration test verifies that the shipped source water profiles (hard_shrimp, moderate, soft_acidic, ro_like) produce meaningfully differentiated initial pH values from the new solver. Add a test that constructs WaterState from each profile and asserts ordering (e.g., hard_shrimp pH > moderate pH > soft_acidic pH) and minimum spread (e.g., at least 0.3 pH units between hardest and softest).

The v2→v3 migration (save.rs:283-314) rescales bicarbonate_mg_total along with all dissolved fields, but normalize_loaded_carbonate_state (save.rs:339-348) unconditionally overwrites it after all migrations complete. The migration rescale of bicarbonate_mg_total is dead work. Consider removing it from the dissolved_fields list with a comment explaining that bicarbonate is now solver-derived, to avoid misleading future migration authors into thinking bicarbonate rescaling is load-bearing.

Fix the exact-zero DIC discontinuity in the carbonate solver. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:145-147` returns `NEUTRAL_FALLBACK` whenever DIC reaches zero, but the same solver returns `pH = 8.5` for arbitrarily small positive DIC under the same alkalinity. Because live update paths clamp DIC to exactly zero before resolving (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:304-313`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:147-149`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs:112-115`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs:193-196`), a strongly photosynthetic tank can jump from the alkaline ceiling to neutral in one tick. The zero-DIC branch should use a limit-consistent fallback instead of snapping to `pH 7.0`.

Unify source-water carbonate validation and runtime resolution onto one authoritative contract. `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:44-46` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:150-169` reject zero-alkalinity / nonzero-DIC source waters via a separate `predicted_carbonate_ph` implementation, while runtime source-water validation in `crates/tank_core/src/types/source_water.rs:31-65` accepts the same chemistry and materialization resolves it through `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-110` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:74-79` / `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:152-156`. Right now the same source-water payload can be rejected when loaded from TOML but accepted when it arrives via a save or runtime catalog, which means preset loading and simulation no longer share one carbonate contract. Move both paths to the same helper/validation rule.
